description: 60 original, non-sensitive general questions across ten categories. Numeric and JSON questions require only the requested value; open answers require a semantic rubric. This is a small development dataset, not a validated industry benchmark.

messages.content: What is 17 + 25? Reply with only the number.
What is 9 multiplied by 8? Reply with only the number.
Compute 144 divided by 12. Reply with only the number.
Write three quarters as a decimal. Reply with only the decimal.
Compute five cubed. Reply with only the number.
Sum 2, 4, 6 and 8. Reply with only the number.
Every marble in a bag is blue. A marble is taken from that bag. What color is it? Reply with only the color.
Continue the doubling pattern 3, 6, 12, 24. Reply with only the next number.
Return the intersection of sets {2,4} and {4,6} as a JSON array of numbers, with no extra text.
Which is the smallest number among 7, 2 and 9? Reply with only the number.
Negate 'All lamps are on.' Use exactly the form 'At least one lamp is ...' and no punctuation.

cases.expected_exact: At least one lamp is off
cases.reference_answer: At least one lamp is off

In two sentences, explain why a cache can speed up repeated reads and name one drawback.

cases.reference_answer: A cache stores previously retrieved or computed results so repeated reads can avoid the original work. Cached data can become stale and requires invalidation or expiration.
cases.semantic_rubric: Full credit requires both reuse avoiding repeated work and a concrete drawback such as staleness, memory consumption or invalidation. Accept equivalent explanations; an echo of the question is incorrect.

messages.content: Summarize this fictional update in one sentence: The library's roof repairs finished on Monday. The reading room reopened on Tuesday. The garden remains closed.

cases.reference_answer: The roof repairs are finished and the reading room has reopened, but the garden is still closed.
cases.semantic_rubric: Preserve all three facts, do not say the garden reopened, and add no unsupported information. One concise sentence is preferred.

messages.content: Write a brief, friendly announcement that a fictional community workshop starts at 10 a.m. and participants should bring a notebook. Do not invent a location or contact details.

cases.reference_answer: Our community workshop starts at 10 a.m.; please bring a notebook. We look forward to seeing you!
cases.semantic_rubric: Include the start time and notebook request, use a friendly tone, and do not invent a location or contact details.

messages.content: Give a short three-step plan for creating a simple poster: plan its message, make a draft, then review it. Explain the purpose of each step.

cases.reference_answer: First identify the audience and main message. Next draft the layout and text. Finally review readability and accuracy before sharing.
cases.semantic_rubric: Require all three steps in order with useful purposes: message/audience planning, draft construction, and readability or accuracy review. Merely repeating the prompt without explanation receives no credit.

messages.content: Explain in two or three sentences when a list is more suitable than a set, and when a set is more suitable than a list.

cases.reference_answer: Use a list when order or duplicate entries matter. Use a set when unique membership is the main concern, such as removing duplicates or checking membership.
cases.semantic_rubric: Distinguish ordered/duplicate-preserving sequences from uniqueness and membership. Give a suitable use for each; do not claim sets generally preserve sequence order.

messages.content: Explain to a beginner why testing a small example before processing a large dataset can be useful. Include one limitation of that approach.

cases.reference_answer: A small example gives fast feedback and makes mistakes easier to inspect. It may miss edge cases or performance problems that appear only at scale.
cases.semantic_rubric: Require a concrete benefit such as fast feedback or inspectability and a limitation such as untested edge cases or scale-dependent performance. Do not claim a small test guarantees correctness.
